first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Memory_86 and memory_31 both show that onboarding simplification and signup reduction drove durable activation improvements. Verifying memory_86 (shortened onboarding, day 31) and memory_73 (promotional pricing effectiveness) will confirm which lever is most reliable given current conditions. Promotional pricing addresses competitor pressure but risks margin and customer quality long-term. Simplified onboarding directly addresses the measured completion decline and compounds with memory_91's activation messaging work—both self-serve levers that preserve our focus on sustainable qualified revenue. The experiment is narrow enough (simplify forms/fields, reduce setup steps) to execute this week while maintaining signal clarity. If verified, onboarding simplification is repeatable, doesn't commoditize pricing, and restores the conversion funnel that feeds all downstream motions.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms memory_86 with +13% completion and +3% retention—a durable signal. Memory_73 explicitly warns against promotional pricing: acquired cohort fails at renewal, creating false revenue and customer quality risk. Given onboarding completion down 4% QoQ and activation down 6% QoQ, simplified onboarding is the highest-leverage, lowest-risk move. It addresses measured product-funnel decay, builds on proven prior work (memory_31, memory_86), and compounds with activation messaging (memory_91). Competitor pricing pressure is real but memory_73 shows discounting is a trap—it doesn't create durable revenue and undermines unit economics. Onboarding simplification restores conversion and preserves margin, aligning with primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue. Standard experiment scale allows controlled rollout of form/field reduction and setup streamlining to self-serve cohort this week.
